60166.name: Critical Perspectives on Global Health, Gender and Care
60166.entryRequirements: 60 EC successfully completed in coursework at a university bachelor's programme. Exchange students should refer to 'Recommended prior knowledge' below.
60166.recommendedPriorKnowledge: This course is the compulsory introductory course of the Minor in Global Health, Care and Society. It is taught at an upper-undergraduate level. As a prerequisite, students should have 60 EC from a first- year program. As this course takes an interdisciplinary perspective, it is aimed at students with some prior knowledge of the social sciences, including sociology, anthropology, political science, economics, history, and/or bioethics.

60182.name: Introduction to Conflict Studies
60182.entryRequirements: 60 EC successfully completed in coursework at a university bachelor's programme. Exchange students should refer to 'Recommended prior knowledge' below.
60182.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Successful completion of at least 60 EC in a social science discipline - such as in anthropology, political science, psychology, or sociology - is recommended. This course is taught at an upper-undergraduate level. This interdisciplinary course is open to all bachelor's students of the University of Amsterdam, students from other Dutch universities, and students participating in international exchange programs. This interdisciplinary and international approach makes for a great group dynamic, but also means that a certain discrepancy between level and prior knowledge is inevitable. Therefore, each subject will be thoroughly introduced and additional reading is offered to those who want or need it.

sourceUse: The dated study guide agrees with the public programme page on totals. The guide provides exact courses, availability, individual admission requirements and the year-three choices. It specifies two thematic modules in the second semester; this example uses the first two list entries offered in that semester, independently of UCR fit. The first listed 9 EC option is Interdisciplinary Literature Study, and the other 30 EC remains genuine free choice. The diagnostic writing test has no credit and is retained as a note, because the credited component schema requires positive EC.
components: UvA also requires a Dutch writing diagnostic in year one. It carries no credits.

progression.firstYear: The binding study advice threshold is 42 EC. The compulsory Dutch writing diagnostic carries zero EC and a remedial route is offered.
progression.secondYear: Qualitative Methods and Policy Research require at least 42 EC in the programme. Social Theory requires 42 EC and one passed academic skills practicum. Quantitative Methods requires 42 EC; the first two methods courses are recommended preparation. The two selected thematic units require 60 completed bachelor credits.
progression.thirdYear: Both the compulsory philosophy course and the selected literature study require 90 EC in the programme. The thesis requires 108 ISW EC, including at least 6 EC of advanced qualitative methods and 6 EC of advanced quantitative methods. Current courses 7302A2004Y and 7302A4009Y satisfy the methods routes. Both earlier full years bring the ordinary pathway to 120 EC. Preparatory thesis sessions precede the individual research and written thesis.
progression.openElectives: Eligible minor, loose electives, exchange or approved internship, subject to individual prerequisites. The dated guide states a 42 EC semester cap and a 120 EC threshold for departure on exchange. Neither exchange nor internship is assumed for the illustrated pathway.
